Each iteration adds the input character value to the accumulator. So I need to reverse this XOR-based check: for each position i, input[i] XOR edx == target_ct[i], where edx starts at 0xbe (lower byte) and gets updated by adding previous input chars.

# target_ct at 0x402060, length 23 (0x17)
target_ct = bytes([0xf8, 0x48, 0x11, 0xd6, 0xa3, 0x30, 0xd3, 0x7f, 
                   0x1e, 0x92, 0x0d, 0xd9, 0x78, 0x08, 0x8e, 0x21,
                   0xcf, 0x70, 0xb6, 0xf6, 0xcf, 0x19, 0x18])

# edx starts at 0xffffffbe, but we only use lower byte for XOR
# Actually, looking at the code:
# - edx = 0xffffffbe (which is -66 as signed, or 0xbe as lower byte)
# - for each char: xor(input[i], edx) == target_ct[i]
# - Then edx += input[i]

# So input[i] = target_ct[i] ^ (edx & 0xff)

edx = 0xffffffbe
result = []
for i in range(23):
    # XOR uses the lower byte of edx
    char = target_ct[i] ^ (edx & 0xff)
    result.append(char)
    # edx is updated by adding the char (as signed addition in 32-bit)
    edx = (edx + char) & 0xffffffff

decoded = bytes(result)
print("Decoded:", decoded)
print("Repr:", repr(decoded))
